title: Rift MCP surface
description: JSON values accepted and returned by the Rift MCP server. Each definition carries the Protobuf identity used after `rift mcp` decodes the request.

rift:entryPoints.description: Tools map MCP request and result JSON to Rift service methods. Resources map each URI family to its template, link, and payload types. Every other schema definition is reachable from one of these entries.

discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.summary: Find code and read what an adapter knows about it. Every answer carries the snapshot it resolved against and how much of the source it covered, so a later call can ask about the same state.

changes.title: Changes
changes.summary: Build a candidate. Each tool resolves one operation against a base or against the candidate named by `on`, writes an immutable commit, and validates it. Nothing reaches a ref or the connection worktree until publication.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle
lifecycle.summary: Continue a retained candidate. `refresh` reruns it on a newer base. `publish` advances a ref after replay and validation, while `persist` copies accepted paths into the connection worktree.

execution.title: Execution
execution.summary: Evaluate caller-provided code against an exact snapshot in a disposable workspace, and inspect the frames a failed evaluation left behind. Host policy authorizes these per language before they are advertised at all.

tree.description: Lists the project tree at one snapshot. Rift derives directories from Git paths and answers without starting a language adapter. A depth of one is an `ls`; an unbounded depth with path selectors is a recursive tree, glob, or file find.

outline.description: Reads the adapter-owned declaration structure of one file. Results preserve source nesting and carry semantic coverage, so an empty outline distinguishes an empty file from an unsupported language.

search.description: Searches symbols, nodes and files in a stable ranked order. A lexical query finds names or text; a structured filter walks adapter facts. Path selectors narrow either form. Every page carries its total order, continuation cursor, and coverage.

match.description: Finds byte ranges. Rift runs literal and regular-expression matching over every UTF-8 file. The owning adapter parses structural patterns because it defines the language's syntax. Every hit carries a key an edit can address.

edit.description: Builds a candidate from an atomic set of concrete edits. Nothing is published: the candidate is an immutable commit that `publish` can advance a ref to.

patch.description: Builds a candidate from a unified diff. Rift checks every hunk's context against the state it resolves against. A patch written for older bytes is refused before any hunk is applied.

rewrite.description: Builds a candidate by replacing every match of one query. The cardinality is checked before expansion, so a pattern that matches more places than intended refuses instead of rewriting them.

revert.description: Builds a candidate from the three-way inverse of one commit against a selected parent.

merge.description: Builds a candidate by merging one exact commit into the candidate state.

rename.description: Changes what a declaration is called and rewrites every reference that names it. The adapter checks spelling, collisions, and binding changes. A reference outside the scope refuses the whole operation.

move.description: Moves a declaration or file to another container or path and updates the imports and references that reach it.

delete.description: Removes a declaration. Without a policy this is a mechanical removal that analyses no references. With one, the adapter classifies every remaining use, applies the stated disposition, and refuses when reference coverage is incomplete.

change_signature.description: Changes the shape of a callable and propagates it to callers, overrides, and implementations. Unlike a rename, it rewrites argument lists, so it commonly raises a `behavior_unknown` confirmation.

act.description: Resolves one action an adapter offered — a quick fix, an extraction, an inline, or an adapter-specific family. Arguments are validated against the schema the offer advertises. A portable family is refused here and resolves through its own tool.

integrate.description: Merges the connection's accepted commit into a local branch and validates the result. Two commits that are each valid can merge into a broken tree, so the merge candidate is validated like any other. A conflict returns a parseable provisional merge.

refresh.description: Reruns a retained candidate's operation against a newer base and reports how much the result moved. The candidate holds the request it was built from, so nothing has to be restated.

publish.description: Runs the declared command validators against a retained candidate and advances its destination by compare-and-swap: the accepted ref for an ordinary candidate, the target branch for an integration. A retry that finds the destination already holding the candidate returns the same result.

persist.description: Materializes an accepted commit into the connection worktree. Each requested path reports its own outcome, so drift, sparse checkout rules, nested repositories, and deletion policy remain visible to the caller.

execute.description: Evaluates a caller-provided code block with one configured language adapter against an exact snapshot. Rift prepares a disposable execution workspace and discards every filesystem write made by the evaluated code.

debug_start.description: Starts an inspect-only debugging evaluation. An unhandled failure retains bounded stack frames until the caller stops the connection-bound session.

debug_get_frame.description: Reads one retained stack frame without resuming evaluation.

debug_stop.description: Releases a debugging session, adapter state, and execution workspace.

repository.description: Reports the tools and resources this workspace serves, which languages have adapters, the state answers resolve against, request limits, retention, and the active conformance profile. Clients read it before calling another entry point.

symbol.description: Returns one symbol at one snapshot with its declaration, source nodes, types, relationships, diagnostics, and coverage. The nodes and relationships identify the references a rename or deletion has to handle.

diff.description: What changed between two revisions, a page of files at a time: the entry on each side and the edits between them. Git answers it without an adapter, so it works for a language Rift has no adapter for.

file.description: One file at one revision: the entry Git records, its language ownership, and one bounded content range. The next URI continues a large regular file.

preview.description: Returns the retained plan behind one candidate, including the request it was built from, its concrete edits, candidate diff, adapter and validator evidence, and confirmations. Its `parent` reads back the chain the candidate belongs to.

actions.description: Returns the fixes and refactors an adapter offers at one address, or across one file. Each entry carries the offer identity and what the action would do, and leaves out the argument schema so a page stays bounded however many offers it holds.

action.description: Returns one discovered action with the JSON Schema of the arguments it takes. This is the read a caller makes for the offer it chose, before handing the same identity to `act`.

rift:axes.description: Each axis owns a set of definitions. `identifiedBy` supplies its roots, then the group closes over references without taking a definition already assigned to another axis. `holds` assigns explicit definitions and `residualOf` assigns the unclaimed definitions from one schema document.

groups.name: Versioning
groups.summary: Revision selectors, resolved snapshots, commits, worktrees, diffs, and retained previews.

groups.name: Filesystem
groups.summary: Project paths, files, syntax-tree nodes, byte ranges, and proposed source edits.

groups.name: Semantic
groups.summary: Adapter-resolved symbols, their types and documentation, and relationships between them.

groups.name: Discovery
groups.summary: Filters, path selectors, and text or structural queries used to find code.

groups.name: Reachability
groups.summary: Coverage, diagnostics, validation reports, and validator output for returned facts.

groups.name: Operations

groups.name: Execution
groups.summary: Caller-provided code evaluation, bounded process output, and connection-bound post-mortem debugging frames.

groups.name: Protocol

ActParams.description: Resolves one discovered adapter action — a quick fix, an extraction, an inline, anything an adapter offers that has no portable contract. Rift validates `arguments` against the offer's advertised schema. An offer whose kind belongs to a portable family is refused here, because `rename`, `move`, `delete`, and `change_signature` are its typed entry points.

rev.description: State against which resolution begins when `on` is absent. Omission selects the connection's current accepted revision.

expected_accepted.description: Accepted-ref head expected at publication. Omission selects the current accepted head. The selected commit must be an ancestor of `rev`.

formatting.description: Formatting applied after this operation's edits resolve.

action.description: The offer to resolve, as the actions resource returned it.

arguments.description: Arguments accepted by the offer's `ActionDescriptor.arguments_schema`. An action with no parameters receives an empty object.

ConformanceProfile.description: Runtime conformance level verified for this workspace. Profiles accumulate. Shared checks validate schemas and examples, reference reachability, axis ownership, generated Protobuf output, adapter service compilation, and the handshake. Runtime fixtures cover ordering, limits, typed failures, the shared-worktree barrier, and topological virtual-source sync. `Contract` identifies the schema under test.

rift:enumDescriptions.edit: Adds `apply` and `integrate` preview, refresh, and publish, the preview resource, adapter formatting, and adapter validation. Fixtures exercise every Change variant and advertised action family, complete validation, preview pagination, refresh comparison, rejected-candidate repair, idempotent retry, compare-and-swap races, integration conflicts and target races, cancellation, and crash recovery. Caller-supplied validators remain unavailable and `max_validators` is zero.
rift:enumDescriptions.full: Adds command validators and `persist` materialization. Fixtures verify response preflight before worktree writes, per-path drift outcomes, direct execution without shell expansion, validation-workspace cleanup, environment construction, timeouts, and bounded output capture. A release claim also runs the suite with two different language adapters and one embedded-language repository.
rift:enumDescriptions.read: Serves the read tools plus repository, symbol, diff, and file resources. Fixtures reconstruct file bytes, verify language summaries and match tags, replay cursors, reject stale state, preserve coverage, and stop at gitlinks. Fixtures cover shared-worktree languages and retained virtual files. Mechanical reads and warm cached semantic reads run with adapters stopped. Fixed repositories record latency, bytes, tokens, and adapter memory.

rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_protocol_error: An adapter contract is unusable. Causes include a malformed message, a field outside its range, ambiguous source or virtual claims, overlapping write claims, a virtual path collision, and a cycle in virtual-source routing. Correct the adapter configuration before retrying.
rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_timeout: The adapter took the call and did not answer inside its budget. Retrying can work: a cold adapter on a large workspace is slow once and fast afterwards.
rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_unavailable: No adapter is running for the language the request names: none is installed, or the one that was has died. A structural query against a language with no adapter lands here.
rift:enumDescriptions.cancelled: The caller cancelled, or the connection went away before the request finished. Sending it again is fine.
rift:enumDescriptions.content_unavailable: The entry is known but its bytes cannot be produced: an LFS object Rift does not fetch, or a blob the object store cannot read. Retrying does not help.
rift:enumDescriptions.cursor_invalid: The cursor is malformed, or it was minted for a different request, order or page size. Start the query again from its first page.
rift:enumDescriptions.cursor_snapshot_mismatch: The cursor is well-formed but the state it was minted against has moved, so continuing it would splice two different answers together. Start again against the current state.
rift:enumDescriptions.deadline_exceeded: The request ran past its time budget. A smaller one may succeed — a lower `limit`, a narrower path selector — and so may the same one once a cold adapter has warmed up.
rift:enumDescriptions.internal_error: A bug in Rift. `causes` says what it was doing at the time, and a retry is not expected to answer differently.
rift:enumDescriptions.invalid_request: The request does not satisfy the schema, or names something the schema forbids: a `limit` above the advertised maximum, a filter field that does not exist. The same bytes fail identically.
rift:enumDescriptions.limit_exceeded: A request or a response crossed an advertised limit. `limit` says which one and by how much, so the request can be resized and sent again.
rift:enumDescriptions.permission_denied: Host policy refused — a path outside the workspace, a revision this deployment does not expose, a language not authorized for execution, or a debugging session owned by another connection. The same request fails the same way.
rift:enumDescriptions.record_reclaimed: The record existed and has been vacuumed away after its retention window. It stays distinct from `resource_not_found` because a retry that read a silent miss would re-run work that already happened. Nothing brings it back.
rift:enumDescriptions.resource_not_found: The identity is well-formed and resolves to nothing — no such symbol, no such file at that revision, or a debug session already stopped or expired. Retrying does not help.
rift:enumDescriptions.revision_not_accepted: The commit exists, but this connection has no accepted publication for it. Publish its preview before asking `persist` to materialize it.
rift:enumDescriptions.semantic_snapshot_mismatch: The snapshot passed back is no longer one the server can answer from — the working tree moved under it, or the adapter that held its facts was restarted. Re-read the current snapshot and rebuild whatever was pinned to the old one.
rift:enumDescriptions.semantic_snapshot_unavailable: The revision resolves, but Rift has no index for it yet: the adapters are still analysing, or that state's facts were dropped. Retrying once indexing catches up succeeds.
rift:enumDescriptions.snapshot_not_found: The revision does not resolve here: a deleted branch, a commit never fetched, a working tree that has been removed. Retrying helps only once the revision exists.
rift:enumDescriptions.storage_failure: Rift could not read or write its own state — the semantic database, the git object store, the socket directory. Worth retrying only if the cause was transient, such as a disk that has since been cleared.
rift:enumDescriptions.unsupported_protocol: The client and server use different protocol versions. Compare `Contract` with the client's supported contract.
rift:enumDescriptions.validator_execution_failure: Rift could not prepare the validation workspace, launch the command validator, enforce its timeout, or capture its output. One retry is reasonable when the host failure was transient.
rift:enumDescriptions.worktree_busy: Another Rift process holds the lease on the working tree this request has to touch. Contention is transient, so the same request retries.

RelationshipFacet.description: One portable category an edge falls into. The local kinds `import` and `use` can share the `imports` facet, which lets one query cross languages.

rift:enumDescriptions.aliases: `from` is another name for `to` — a type alias, a re-export, an `as` rename.
rift:enumDescriptions.annotated_by: `to` is attached to `from` as metadata: an annotation, a decorator, an attribute.
rift:enumDescriptions.augments: `from` adds members to `to`, which is declared elsewhere — a Rust `impl` block, a TypeScript `declare module`, an `ALTER TABLE`, a CSS rule for a selector another file already styles.
rift:enumDescriptions.binds: `from` names `to` across a language boundary: a `className` and the CSS rule it selects, an ORM entity and its table.
rift:enumDescriptions.bounded_by: `from` is constrained to satisfy `to` — the `Serialize` in `T: Serialize`, the `Comparable` in `<T extends Comparable<T>>`.
rift:enumDescriptions.catches: `from` handles `to` when something it calls raises it.
rift:enumDescriptions.configures: `from` supplies configuration `to` reads — a `rift.toml` key and the field it fills, a `tsconfig` path alias and the module it resolves.
rift:enumDescriptions.contains: `from` lexically holds `to` — a module and the functions written in it.
rift:enumDescriptions.declares: `from` owns `to`. A class carries this to its methods even where the language writes them outside its body.
rift:enumDescriptions.depends_on: `from` needs `to` and there is no place in the source to point at — a manifest entry, a build dependency. The coarsest edge there is.
rift:enumDescriptions.embeds: `from` holds `to` and promotes its members, so they are reachable without naming the field. Go struct embedding.
rift:enumDescriptions.generates: `to` was produced from `from` by a build step, so editing `to` lasts until the next build.
rift:enumDescriptions.has_type: `to` is the type of `from`. What jump-to-type-definition follows.
rift:enumDescriptions.imports: `from` brings `to` in from another unit. A header or a stylesheet that declares nothing of its own is a synthetic `module` symbol, so `#include` and `@import` are the same edge as a Python `import`.
rift:enumDescriptions.instantiates: `from` applies `to` as a type argument — the `Config` in `Vec<Config>`.
rift:enumDescriptions.mixes_in: `from` takes members from `to` by linearization — a Dart `with` clause, a Scala mixin. The order they are written in decides which one wins.
rift:enumDescriptions.overloads: `from` and `to` share a name and differ in signature, and the language picks between them at the call site.
rift:enumDescriptions.reads: `from` takes the value of `to`. A SQL `SELECT` against a table is this edge.
rift:enumDescriptions.references: `from` mentions `to` somewhere in the source and nothing narrower fits. The fallback edge where there is a node to point at.
rift:enumDescriptions.specializes: `from` is a narrower form of `to`, chosen over it where both match.
rift:enumDescriptions.tests: `from` exercises `to`. A test that reaches its target through reflection or HTTP has no call edge to carry it.
rift:enumDescriptions.writes: `from` assigns to `to`. A SQL `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE` is this edge.

RevertParams.description: A validated three-way inverse of one commit. Rift computes the difference from `parent` to `revision`, applies its inverse, and refuses overlapping changes it cannot merge without guessing.

on.description: Retained candidate this operation continues. Omission starts from `rev`. The operation resolves against that candidate's tree, so a rename can follow the edit that created what it renames, and the chain is the transaction.

rev.description: State against which resolution begins when `on` is absent. Omission selects the connection's current accepted revision.

expected_accepted.description: Accepted-ref head expected at publication. Omission selects the current accepted head. The selected commit must be an ancestor of `rev`.

formatting.description: Formatting applied after this operation's edits resolve.

revision.description: Exact commit whose changes are inverted.

parent.description: Parent against which the commit's change is defined. Required for ordinary and merge commits; null selects the empty tree for a root commit. A commit that does not have this parent is refused.

paths.description: Paths from the original commit eligible for inversion. Excluded paths remain untouched; the commit diff exposes them when the caller needs to inspect the omission.

RevertParams.title: RevertParams

Revision.description:
Which state to answer against. Absent, the default branch at its latest commit.

A git revision parameter, as gitrevisions(7) defines one: `main`, `v1.2.0`, `dae86e1`, `HEAD~3`. Dropping the `/HEAD` from a worktree ref addresses what is on disk there, uncommitted edits included, which gitrevisions cannot spell and is what an agent editing code usually means.
Revision.title: Revision

RewriteParams.description: An atomic query-and-rewrite. Rift finds every match, checks the cardinality, expands the replacement, and either applies all resulting edits or refuses the candidate.

on.description: Retained candidate this operation continues. Omission starts from `rev`. The operation resolves against that candidate's tree, so a rename can follow the edit that created what it renames, and the chain is the transaction.

rev.description: State against which resolution begins when `on` is absent. Omission selects the connection's current accepted revision.

expected_accepted.description: Accepted-ref head expected at publication. Omission selects the current accepted head. The selected commit must be an ancestor of `rev`.

formatting.description: Formatting applied after this operation's edits resolve.

query.description: The text or structural pattern evaluated against the state this operation resolves against.

replacement.description: UTF-8 replacement template. `${NAME}` inserts the source bound by a named or numeric capture, `${0}` inserts the whole match, and `$$` inserts one dollar sign. An absent capture refuses the rewrite.
replacement.title: Replacement

cardinality.description: The accepted number of matches before expansion.

RewriteParams.title: RewriteParams

RewriteRange.description: Which safe structural range is replaced. Text queries accept `exact` only because they have no grammar-owned trivia boundaries.
RewriteRange.title: RewriteRange

policy.description: Required behavior for every classified remaining use. Null removes the declaration without reference analysis, which claims no reference guarantee and reports no remaining-usage precondition.

scope.description: Source in which complete usage analysis and any requested rewrite may occur.

Complete reference coverage is mandatory.

SafeDeletePolicyReads.description: Disposition for reads, calls, and constructions.

SearchParams.description: What to search for. At least one of `query` and `filter` is required: `query` is lexical, while `filter` is a predicate over adapter facts. `paths` narrows either form before matching.

order.description: Which total order the page comes back in. The cursor is bound to it, so it cannot change between pages of one query.

query.description: Text to match against file contents, symbol names, and rendered signatures. `parse` matches that word in those fields. Caller lookup uses a relationship filter.

filter.description: A predicate over resolved fields and relationships. This is where adapter knowledge enters a search — implements this trait, called by that function, declared under `src/api`.

paths.description: Files eligible for the search, selected by project-relative Git globs. Omitted selects every visible file.

include.description: Extra payload to attach to every hit. Each entry costs a lookup per hit, so ask for what you will read.

limit.description: Most hits to return in one page. `max_page_items` from the repository resource caps it, and fewer may come back.

cursor.description: Continues a previous search where its last page ended. Omit it for the first page; everything else in the request has to match what the cursor was minted for.

rift:enumDescriptions.hint: A suggestion, usually with a code action behind it.

receiver.description: The implicit first parameter — `self`, `this`. Null for a free function, and for languages that have no such thing.

Snapshot.description:
What a `Revision` resolved to, reported beside every answer so a second call can ask the same question again and get the same state.

A commit names its immutable tree. A working-tree snapshot names its base commit and digests the changed set, leaving every unedited file's identity in the base.

oneOf.description: A commit. Nothing about it can change, so the object ID is the whole of the state.

commit.description: The object ID the revision resolved to.

oneOf.title: SnapshotCommit

oneOf.description: A working tree, which changes under you while you read it. It is reported as the commit it sits on plus a digest of what differs, so a second call can tell whether the disk moved.

worktree.description: Which working tree on disk, in the spelling git uses to reach one from another.

base.description: The commit this working tree sits on.

changes.description: What makes this snapshot an identity: two reads of one dirty tree on the same `base` are otherwise indistinguishable. The changed set has no bound. This field is SHA-256 over each differing path with the digest of its content, in RFC 8785 canonical JSON. A clean tree digests the empty set.

oneOf.title: SnapshotWorktree

StructuralCaptureConstraint.description: A condition one capture of a `StructuralQuery` has to meet. Constraints are where a pattern over syntax reaches the adapter's knowledge: match every call, then keep only the ones whose target carries the `test` facet.

capture.description: Which metavariable of the pattern this constrains, written without the `$`.
capture.title: Capture

exact_kind.description: The syntax kind the captured node has to be, in its grammar's own words.

facet.description: A portable structural facet the captured node has to carry.

text_regex.description: A `rift-regex` expression the capture's text must match. Rift evaluates it with Unicode character classes, linear-time matching, and no look-around or backreferences.
text_regex.title: Text Regex

semantic.description: What has to be true of the symbol written at the capture. The adapter matches syntax; Rift applies this, because only Rift holds the resolved facts.

StructuralCaptureConstraintCardinality.description: How many nodes the capture binds, which follows the sigil used in the pattern.

StructuralMatchRanges.description: The ranges a replacement can be written over, computed by the adapter that parsed the match. exact.description: The node itself, with nothing around it. What a replacement in place writes over.

leading.description: The node with the trivia in front of it: the indentation on its line, a separator that precedes it.

trailing.description: The node with what follows it: a trailing comma, the newline that ends its line.

both.description: The node with the trivia on either side. Deleting this leaves no blank line and no orphaned separator.

StructuralQuery.description: A syntax search parsed with the target language's grammar. `$NAME` stands for one node and `$$$NAME` for a run of nodes. Each adapter uses the shared capture, constraint, and result shapes.

version.description: Which revision of the metavariable grammar the pattern is written in.

language.description: Which grammar parses `pattern`, and so which adapter runs the search.

pattern.description: The pattern, in the target language's own syntax, with metavariables where the shape matters and the text does not.

within.description: Optional source boundary for the search. A symbol selects its nodes. A node selects its syntax subtree. A span selects its bytes.

constraints.description: Conditions the captures have to meet. The pattern finds a shape; these narrow it to the occurrences you meant.

extensions.description: Query fields the model has no place for, namespaced by the adapter that reads them.

Symbol.description: Adapter-resolved semantic identity. Source structure lives in Node and is connected through Relationship.

id.description: Unique identifier of this symbol across the whole workspace, and the URI that resolves it. Hand it to the symbol resource as it stands.

language.description: The language this symbol belongs to.

name.description: The human-readable name, as written in the source: `parseConfig`. Rendered signatures live in `signatures`.
name.title: Name

kind.description: What this symbol is in the adapter's vocabulary, such as `trait`, `function`, or `table`.

facets.description: Portable classification for cross-language queries. The local kinds `trait` and `interface` can both carry the `type` facet.
facets.title: Facets

origin.description: Where the symbol comes from: code in this workspace, or a package it depends on.

container.description: The symbol this one belongs to — the class that owns a method, the module that owns a function. Ownership is not lexical: a Go method is written beside its type and a Rust method inside an `impl` block, and both name the type here. Absent at the top level.

visibility.description: How widely the symbol is visible, in the language's own terms — `public`, `private`, `pub(crate)`. Null where the language has no such concept.
visibility.title: Visibility

types.description: The types this symbol carries, each tagged with the role it plays: a return type, a field type, a bound.
types.title: Types

signatures.description: One entry per callable form. Where the language dispatches overloads separately they are separate symbols joined by the `overloads` edge; several entries here are alternative forms of one dispatch target, as `typing.overload` writes them.
signatures.title: Signatures

documentation.description: Doc comments attached to the declaration, with the markup format they were written in.
documentation.title: Documentation

extensions.description: Language-specific facts with no portable equivalent, namespaced by the adapter that emitted them.

document_local.description: Whether language semantics confine this symbol to the document that declares it. The adapter classifies locality from its language model.
document_local.title: Document Local

Symbol.title: Symbol

SymbolFacet.description: One portable category a symbol falls into. Kinds are language-specific; facets are shared, so a filter written once applies to every language an adapter is installed for.

rift:enumDescriptions.abstract: Declared without an implementation. Whatever carries `implements` or `extends` to it has to supply one.
rift:enumDescriptions.alias: Another name for a symbol declared elsewhere — a `typealias`, a C++ `using`, a re-export. The `aliases` edge says which symbol.
rift:enumDescriptions.annotation: Declared to be attached to another declaration: a Java `@interface`, a Kotlin `annotation class`, a Python decorator, a Rust attribute macro.
rift:enumDescriptions.async: Produces a value that completes later. `Signature.effects` keeps the language's own keyword: `async`, `suspend`.
rift:enumDescriptions.callable: Can be called, and so carries at least one `Signature`.
rift:enumDescriptions.constructor: The callable that produces an instance. `constructible` marks the type it produces.
rift:enumDescriptions.deprecated: Marked as no longer to be used, however the language spells it — `@Deprecated`, `#[deprecated]`, a doc tag.
rift:enumDescriptions.entrypoint: Where execution starts: `fn main`, `func main`, a `bin` script named by the package manifest.
rift:enumDescriptions.enumeration: Declares the closed set those variants belong to. A `match` over it is exhaustive once every variant is covered.
rift:enumDescriptions.extensible: Can be inherited from or overridden: a non-`final` class, a Kotlin `open fun`, a C++ `virtual` method.
rift:enumDescriptions.extension: Attached to a type declared somewhere else — a Kotlin extension function, a method in a Rust `impl` block, a Go method, a Dart extension.
rift:enumDescriptions.generator: Yields a sequence one value at a time instead of returning once — a Python generator, a Dart `sync*` function.
rift:enumDescriptions.implementable: Names a contract another type can satisfy: an interface, a trait, a protocol.
rift:enumDescriptions.macro: Expands source at compile time, as `macro_rules!` and preprocessor definitions do.
rift:enumDescriptions.member: Owned by another symbol — a method, a field, an enum variant. Ownership is not lexical: a Go method is written beside its type, and a Rust method inside an `impl` block.
rift:enumDescriptions.member_container: Can hold members: a class, a struct, an interface.
rift:enumDescriptions.module: A unit the language imports whole. A TypeScript file carries this facet, and so do a Rust `mod` and a Go package, both of which can span several files.
rift:enumDescriptions.mutable: Can be reassigned after it is initialized. A Rust `let mut` carries it, a `let` does not.
rift:enumDescriptions.namespace: Groups names without being a unit the language loads — a C++ `namespace`, a Java package, a SQL schema.
rift:enumDescriptions.operator: Invoked through operator syntax — C++ `operator+`, Python `__add__`, a Kotlin `operator fun`.
rift:enumDescriptions.parameter: A parameter of a callable, declared as a symbol of its own so it can be renamed and referred to.
rift:enumDescriptions.property: Read and written as a value, and backed by code that runs — a Kotlin property, a Python `@property`, a JavaScript getter.
rift:enumDescriptions.public: Reachable from outside the unit that declares it. `visibility` carries the language's own word, which Go and Python do not have: there the adapter reads the naming convention.
rift:enumDescriptions.static: Bound to the declaration rather than to an instance, so a call needs no receiver.
rift:enumDescriptions.test: The language's test tooling collects it as a test: a `#[test]` function, a `describe` block.
rift:enumDescriptions.type: Declares a type. `struct Config` and `interface Props` both qualify, which is what makes one search for types find both.
rift:enumDescriptions.type_parameter: A generic parameter — the `T` in `Vec<T>`. A Rust lifetime and a C++ `template<int N>` carry it too.
rift:enumDescriptions.value: Names something that exists while the program runs: a variable, a constant, a function object. A CSS class selector and a SQL sequence carry it too.
rift:enumDescriptions.variant: One case of a closed set: a Rust enum variant, a Scala `case`, a Java enum constant.

SymbolId.description: Identity and resource URI of one symbol. The first path segment is the language name followed by `:<dialect>` when present. The adapter supplies the remaining qualified name and percent-encodes UTF-8 bytes outside URI path characters with uppercase hex. Where a namespace declares identical names, the adapter appends `~` and an index. A revision can be attached as `?rev=`.

SymbolOrigin.description: Source of a symbol definition. The variant determines whether its source can be read or edited and whether a package upgrade can replace it.

oneOf.description: Declared in this workspace's own source. The code you can open and change.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginWorkspace

oneOf.description: Declared in a dependency. `manager` is the package manager that installed it, so `npm`, `cargo` or `pip`; `name` and `version` are that manager's own. Upgrading the dependency replaces these symbols.

manager.description: The package manager that installed it.
manager.title: Manager

name.description: The package name, as that manager spells it.
name.title: Name

oneOf.title: SymbolOriginPackage

oneOf.description: Declared in the language's standard library and installed with its toolchain.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginStdlib

oneOf.description: Declared outside the workspace, its packages, and the language's standard library.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginExternal

oneOf.description: Produced by a build step. Editing it lasts only until it is generated again.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginGenerated

oneOf.description: Invented by the adapter, with no source declaration to read or edit.
oneOf.title: SymbolOriginSynthetic

SymbolResourcePayload.description: JSON payload for one symbol at one snapshot.

uri.description: The symbol this payload answers for, echoed back so a link and its content carry the same address.

at.description: The snapshot this answer was resolved against. Pass it back as `rev` when a later call has to agree with this one.

symbol.description: The declaration itself: its name, its kind in the language's own words, its origin, its types and its signatures.

origin_mappings.description: Relations from produced declaration bytes to source ranges a caller can inspect or edit. Empty for a declaration read directly from physical source.
origin_mappings.title: Origin Mappings

nodes.description: Every place this symbol is written — the declaration and each mention. This is the list a rename has to rewrite.
nodes.title: Nodes

relationships.description: Edges into and out of this symbol, each carrying the nodes from which the adapter derived it.
relationships.title: Relationships

source.description: The source at each node, so the declaration and its call sites can be read without a second round trip.
source.title: Source

diagnostics.description: What the adapter reported at this symbol's nodes.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

coverage.description: How complete each fact family is for this symbol. An empty `relationships` means the symbol has no edges only where that family is complete.

next.description: The same symbol URI carrying the cursor for the next page, or null on the last one. Nodes, edges and diagnostics are what page.

SymbolResourcePayload.title: SymbolResourcePayload

TextEdit.description: One byte range of one file, and what replaces it. Offsets are into the file as it stands at the pinned snapshot, so edits in a set never observe each other, and two of them may not overlap.

span.description: The file, and the byte range being replaced.

text.description: What the range becomes. Empty deletes it.
text.title: Text

TextEdit.title: TextEdit

TextQuery.description: Literal or regular-expression matching over any UTF-8 file. Rift evaluates this query even when no adapter claims the path. Matches are leftmost-first and non-overlapping. After an empty regular-expression match, scanning advances to the next UTF-8 boundary. The query carries its dialect so a stored match key remains self-contained.

version.description: Version of the query shape and pattern semantics.
version.title: Version

dialect.description: Regular-expression grammar used in `regex` mode. The separate `version` field selects its syntax and match semantics. Version 1 has Unicode character classes, linear-time matching, and no look-around or backreferences. Protocol conformance fixtures define accepted syntax and match selection.
dialect.title: Dialect

pattern.description: Text to find in the selected grammar.
pattern.title: Pattern

case_sensitive.description: Initial case-sensitivity for regular-expression mode. Inline flags may change it within the pattern.
case_sensitive.title: Case Sensitive

multiline.description: Whether `^` and `$` initially match line boundaries in regular-expression mode. Inline flags may change it within the pattern.
multiline.title: Multiline

TextQuery.title: TextQuery

rift:enumDescriptions.literal: Match the pattern bytewise, with no special characters or flags.
rift:enumDescriptions.regex: Read the pattern using the advertised text-matching dialect and the initial flags below.

TextRange.description: Half-open UTF-8 byte offsets over authoritative UTF-8 source. Every adapter converts from its adapter's native offsets at the seam. No JSON Schema keyword can tie one field to another, so that `end` is never below `start` is asserted by the conformance tests instead.

start.description: First byte of the range, counted from the start of the file.
start.title: Start

end.description: One past the last byte. Equal to `start` for an empty range, which is how a position between two bytes is spelled.
end.title: End

TextRange.title: TextRange

TreeParams.description: Selects a portion of the project tree. The root controls hierarchy and `paths` filters the full project-relative path of each descendant.

root.description: Directory whose descendants are listed. The empty path selects the project root; the root entry itself is not returned. A gitlink is a file entry and cannot be used as a directory root.

depth.description: Most directory edges below `root` to include. One lists immediate children; null walks every descendant and relies on pagination and response limits.
depth.title: Depth

paths.description: Git-style include and exclude globs matched against each full project-relative descendant path.

limit.description: Most entries to return in one page. The server may stop earlier to keep the serialized result within `max_response_bytes`.
limit.title: Limit

cursor.description: Continues the same tree walk. Root, depth, paths, revision, and page size remain fixed.

TreeParams.title: TreeParams

TreeResult.description: One page of a project tree, ordered by project-path UTF-8 bytes. A directory precedes a file at the same path, though a valid snapshot normally contains only one.

entries.description: Derived directories and Git entries on this page.
entries.title: Entries

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next path page, or null after the final entry.

TreeResult.title: TreeResult

TypeBinding.description: One type a symbol carries, together with the role it plays for that symbol.
TypeBinding.title: TypeBinding

TypeBindingProvenance.description: Where the type fact came from. A declared type and an inferred one can both be present and disagree, which is the interesting case.

rift:enumDescriptions.declared: Written in the source by the author.
rift:enumDescriptions.expected: What the surrounding context demands here. A mismatch is reported against this one.
rift:enumDescriptions.inferred: The adapter worked it out; nothing in the source says it.

TypeBindingProvenance.title: TypeBindingProvenance

TypeBindingRole.description: What this type is to the symbol that carries it.

rift:enumDescriptions.awaited: What completes inside an asynchronous value — the `T` in `Promise<T>`.
rift:enumDescriptions.bound: A constraint the type has to satisfy — the `Serialize` in `T: Serialize`.
rift:enumDescriptions.discriminant: The representation an enumeration is stored as, where the language pins one.
rift:enumDescriptions.element: What a container holds: the `u8` in `Vec<u8>`, the value type of a map.
rift:enumDescriptions.error: The failure type — the `E` in `Result<T, E>`, a Go `error` return.
rift:enumDescriptions.field: The type of a data member.
rift:enumDescriptions.key: The key type of a map.
rift:enumDescriptions.parameter: The type of an argument the callable takes.
rift:enumDescriptions.receiver: The type of the implicit first argument — `self`, `this`.
rift:enumDescriptions.underlying: What an alias or a newtype wraps.
rift:enumDescriptions.yielded: What a generator produces per step.

TypeBindingRole.title: TypeBindingRole

TypeExpression.description: How a type is written in the source, plus the symbol that declares it when one does. A type with a declaration resolves to that symbol; a structural type — `string | null`, `{ a: string }` — has the spelling and nothing to resolve to.

language.description: The language the spelling is in, and so the adapter that produced it.

source.description: The type as it is written: `Optional[Config]`, `&mut [u8]`, `string | null`.
source.title: Source

resolved.description: The symbol that declares this type, where one does. Null for a structural type, which has a spelling and nothing to open.

extensions.description: Type facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the adapter that emitted them.

TypeExpression.title: TypeExpression

ValidationReport.description: One adapter's verdict over a candidate snapshot. `coverage` states how much the adapter checked, while `valid` records whether the checked scope contains an error. Workspace validation policy decides which reports publication requires.

language.description: The adapter that produced this verdict.

valid.description: Whether this adapter accepted every file in `files` under the reported coverage.
valid.title: Valid

coverage.description: How much of the affected program the adapter checked. Publication refuses partial or unsupported coverage when workspace policy requires this language.

files.description: Affected files this verdict covers, sorted by project path.
files.title: Files

diagnostics.description: Adapter findings produced while checking the candidate, sorted by file and source range.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

ValidationReport.title: ValidationReport

ValidatorResult.description: The completed outcome of one declared validator. Exit status zero passes. Every other exit status fails. A workspace, launch, timeout, or capture failure raises `validator_execution_failure` before Rift produces candidate evidence.

oneOf.description: A declared validator process that exited with status zero.

declaration_digest.description: SHA-256 of the validator's RFC 8785 canonical JSON declaration. Results and declarations form a bijection on this value, because labels may repeat while commands differ.

files.description: Paths evaluated by the validator, sorted by UTF-8 bytes and without duplicates.
files.title: Files

diagnostics.description: Structured findings produced by the validator. The list is empty when its output has no configured diagnostic decoder.

stdout.description: Bounded standard output from the process.

stderr.description: Bounded standard error from the process.
